method: No playback. I metered mix/master.wav (mix 2026-10-14T01:41Z, 2168.4167 s; it postdates the m19 v22 render at 00:41Z and the m02 render at 00:47Z) and narration/narration.wav with ffmpeg ebur128 momentary readings every 0.1-0.3 s, and with 25 ms RMS windows on the how-far stamp. Windows: the L0220 gap (194.4-199.6), all of L1502 (1926.4-1942.8), L1504b, L1505 and the m19 breath (1971.8-1982.8), the two lab blooms (2011.8, 2029.4, 2037.3-2045.2), the m20 to m21 hand-off (2065.5-2072.5), the final stamp and lamp (2125.5-2130) and the end cards (2155-2168.4). summary: Every sound note from round 5 landed and measures right on the master. The how-far stamp is now tucked under 'open', adding at most about 3 dB for about 50 ms, where it used to cover the vowel by 6-12 dB. m19 gives 'Nobody told it... to plan' a true silence on both sides of the new 'Snuff that plan out' line. After 'plan' comes a real breath: 0.3 s of air, an 0.8 s bow to -20.8 M, and gone before 'The candle'. Pitts's line now gets a full second of room tone before the X-ray D, which lands with the picture's X-ray band. The Nobel sentence is now three clean sentences at 156 wpm with WER 0, so 'he wrote' can only be Hopfield. The clock shift moved m20 and m21 without a seam: the lab blooms stay within 1 dB of each other, there is an earned 1.5 s of room tone after Widrow's death, and the ending still rings down to the floor at black. The mix is clean: -16 LUFS, -2 dBTP, LRA 6, about 1.2 dB of master limiting on speech only, every line at least 10.9 dB over the music, and every fade at least 1.6 s after its last strike. Sound still stops at 8.5 rather than 9 for two reasons. No person has yet confirmed how the narrator says seven real names (sixth round). And a small cluster of lines still runs at 190-199 wpm against directions that ask for slow and clear, mostly in the Florence deep dive (L0830 199 wpm, L0806 195) and on the prologue's riddle (L0105 191 wpm, 'long pause after'). The clock has 3.58 s of headroom, which is enough to slow the two or three that matter most.

issues.fix: Before publish, a person runs `npm run film:voice -- listen --slug neural-net-history`, plays the seven clips, and records each with `film:voice signoff --slug neural-net-history --term <term> --by <name> --verdict ok|reject` so clipSig is set. A rejection becomes a SOLO retake with a lexicon respelling and a T.word re-fit of that line's shot. This is a hand-off, not a gate blocker.

issues.problem: The dropout line in the Florence deep dive ('In the great halls, they snuffed a random half each time, so no lantern could count on another. Like a team where anyone might be missing, each had to know the work.') runs 9.64 s at 199 wpm, the fastest line in the film. Its direction is 'slow and clear; let each time be heard; count on another said simply'. It is the only explanation of dropout, and it sits in a run of fast lines in the same chapter (L0806 195, L0816 195, L0817 192, L0825 198), so the densest teaching is also the quickest narration.

The added time (about +1.4 s) fits in the 3.58 s headroom (2168.42 of 2172). Re-fit ch08-s08b by T.word ('snuffed', 'another', 'missing', 'work'), shift m10's hits after the line by the measured delta, rebuild the clock once, and re-mix. If the take sounds slowed or sing-song, keep the current one.
